title: New Beginnings in Bridgehampton
summary: Explore Target’s new Bridgehampton store, featuring thoughtful design, localized merchandising and a guest experience inspired by the Hamptons.
body_markdown:
Gray shingles, white trim, soft florals and a beachy vibe — it’s the quintessential Hamptons house, and the inspiration for one of Target’s newest stores.


This October, we opened our first store on eastern Long Island’s East End, in the hamlet of Bridgehampton, New York. It’s a journey that started more than seven years ago, when we were searching for a site that would allow us to serve guests in the coastal community.


“It’s really hard to find sites that will work for Target, but the market, the demand has always been there,” says **Brandt U.** , regional real estate director, of the Long Island area. The closest Target was in Riverhead, about an hour-plus drive away. That’s when our real estate team found the perfect opportunity — a 90,000-square-foot building in the only large shopping center in the Hamptons.


> There truly was one site that would work for us.
>
>
> Brandt U.
>
>
> Regional Real Estate Director, Target


This was just the start of a multiyear effort by our real estate, construction, store design, merchandising and operations team members to give Bridgehampton its first Target.


“I’m one of the few people that sees it from the very inception of an idea of a store there, all the way to handing it over to the store team and watching them putting the final touches on to open it to our guests,” says **Genevieve M.** , senior project manager, construction. “The build out, figuring out, solving problems and watching the transformation — we are very lucky to have teams that like to collaborate. It makes the job a whole lot more fun to do and get up every morning.”


Our Bridgehampton store is one of[eight new stores](https://corporate.target.com/press/fact-sheet/2024/04/store-openings) we’re opening this fall — each one delivering Target’s style, design and value, elevated guest experience, and good paying jobs. For Bridgehampton, the path to opening day came with a unique twist: transforming the existing space into a store that delivers the Target experience while still reflecting the beach community.


### Designed to delight


While Target approaches most new stores based on a standard prototype, we also can flex with the needs of a community. For example, in San Clemente, California, we worked with the local design board to create an external design that complemented the city’s white stucco, red clay-tile roofed Spanish Colonial Revival architecture.


“It’s all about building an emotional connection,” says **Ken M.** , principal architect of store design, “and making guests want to come back and feel like you understand their community and that you’re happy to be part of their community.”


In Bridgehampton, that meant working within the town’s design guidelines, which emphasized an understated, coastal aesthetic, while letting the Target brand shine through. The store design team — made up of architects, graphic and interior designers, and store planners — found their inspiration in the “Hamptons house.”


The team crafted an exterior design that connects the building to its community — think gray shingles trimmed in white. Other design touches inside completed the transformation.


Previous slide


-


**Built for Bridgehampton:** While the typical store sign glows Target red, the approved exterior palette in Bridgehampton is limited to blue and white, while signage can only have external lighting. So, the Target team designed a white bullseye logo that is lit from above, and pops against the gray backdrop of the building. Similarly, we painted our iconic round bollards gray instead of red to fit within guidelines.


-


**View to a thrill:** Since Target branding on the outside of the store is restrained, we opened up the building’s front wall, adding more windows so people outside can see the activity, light and displays at the front of the store. It’s about “letting our brand flow out,” as Ken describes it, “so that people could see the real Target inside.”


-


**Sit a spell:** A front porch element with Adirondack chairs, planters with native plants and trellises greet guests, providing a new gathering place. While the city typically does not allow these elements in front of a store, the Target team met with leaders “to explain that we are trying to encourage people to slow down, stop and enjoy the moment,” says Genevieve. “This is an added benefit for the community.”


-


**Fitting room cabana:** The creative team designed each fitting room as a beach cabana with small porthole mirrors on the doors, coastal artwork and shutters. “Because it's a smaller piece of the store, you could really dive in and make it something special,” Ken says.


-


**Wallpaper whimsy:** For the fitting rooms, Target’s creative team designed a custom wall covering inspired by the toile wallpaper frequently found in the Hamptons — but with a Bullseye spin. “As a local guest goes into the fitting room, they may not even see it at first,” says Ken of the images of our mascot frolicking around Bridgehampton landmarks. “Then they start looking closer and seeing all these little surprise moments. It’s all about delighting our guests.”


-


**Coastal touches:** Wicker globe light shades, walnut benches, custom coat hooks and mirrors, and stenciled waves on the store’s concrete floor add another level of local flavor to the store. “The most joy from Bridgehampton was actually getting to do the elevated design,” says Genevieve, “because it took it from just a Target to a Target that belongs in the Hamptons.”


Next slide


The goal for all these design touches: Make Target’s Bridgehampton store timeless, so that it can bring joy to guests for years to come. “The design fits into the pillars that we always try to maintain: You want to be current, you want to be on trend, but you also don't want to be too far out there that in two years it's dated,” Ken says.


### Building a new team


Turnover Day — when the contractor turns over the keys of our new store to its new team — is always memorable. For **Adriana F.** , store director for Bridgehampton, it was also an opportunity to see the end result of those many years of hard work.


“My first impression of the Bridgehampton store is it just feels like the Hamptons, but also just feels like Target,” she says.


And now, it’s time for the store’s team to fully bring Target’s elevated guest experience to life.


Bridgehampton’s Target: It puts us one step closer to our goal of having more than 2,300 stores by 2035 across the United States. It’s a one-stop shop for guests to find Target’s style, design and value; a launchpad for its team to build rewarding careers; and a new gathering place for the community.
